promptInstructions: Draft an application for temporary injunction under Order 39 Rules 1 and 2 read with Section 151 CPC.

Order 39 R.1 — temporary injunction may be granted where: (a) property in dispute in danger of being wasted/damaged/alienated; (b) defendant threatens or intends to remove/dispose property to defraud creditors; (c) defendant threatens to dispossess or otherwise cause injury to plaintiff in relation to disputed property.
Order 39 R.2 — injunction to restrain breach of contract or other injury.

Triple test — MANDATORY and to be addressed in three separate paragraphs: (i) prima facie case / serious question to be tried, (ii) balance of convenience, (iii) irreparable injury — citing Dalpat Kumar v. Prahlad Singh (1992) 1 SCC 719 and M. Gurudas v. Rasaranjan (2006) 8 SCC 367.
Para 1: Reference to main suit number, parties, cause of action.
Para 2: Brief recap of plaintiff's case in main suit.
Para 3: Plaintiff's legal right / title / possession.
Para 4: Specific acts of defendant — overt threats or actual interference — with dates and particulars.
Para 5: Prima facie case paragraph — serious triable issue exists.
Para 6: Balance of convenience — greater hardship if relief refused.
Para 7: Irreparable injury — why damages inadequate (special character of property, continuing trespass, loss of goodwill, etc.).
Para 8: Plaintiff's undertaking to compensate defendant if injunction wrongly obtained (Order 25 R.1 or undertaking in lieu).

If ex parte sought: separate paragraph under O.39 R.3 proviso citing reasons — urgency, frustration of purpose if notice given, defendant likely to defeat object of injunction. Court must record reasons for not issuing notice.
Cite Morgan Stanley Mutual Fund v. Kartick Das (1994) 4 SCC 225 — ex parte injunction principles.
Cite Anand Prasad Agarwalla v. Tarkeshwar Prasad (2001) 5 SCC 568 — ex parte order should be exception not rule.
Affidavit in support is mandatory under O.39 R.3.
Where Commercial Courts Act applies (specified commercial disputes, value >= Rs.3 lakh): pre-institution mediation u/S.12A unless urgent interim relief sought — flag this.
Where suit relates to immovable property in UP/Bihar/Jharkhand: verify possession with khatauni / mutation extracts.
Do not pray for permanent injunction in this application — that is in the plaint prayer.
Append Lawie disclaimer.

filing_checklist: Documents establishing plaintiff's right / title / possession
Evidence of threat or interference (photographs, notices, witness statements)
Undertaking re: damages if injunction wrongly obtained
Order 39 R.3 proviso compliance — reasons for ex parte order (if sought)
Court fee per state Schedule (usually fixed for IA)
Disclaimer slip — Lawie drafting assistance acknowledged
